si_4_title: Beyond homogeneity: charting the landscape of heterogeneity in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric electroencephalography
sc_1_study_objective: This study combines high-density EEG with normative modeling to quantify electrophysiological heterogeneity using spectral power and functional connectivity across a cohort of 1674 patients with neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders (ADHD, ASD, LD, ANX) and 560 matched controls, aiming to enhance comparative analysis and identify patient-specific markers for precision psychiatry.

rci_7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Bandpass filtering (1-100 Hz); Downsampling (200 Hz); Bad channel identification (pyprep algorithm, RANSAC-based); Interpolation (neighboring electrodes); Re-referencing (common average reference); ICA (IClabel algorithm); Second bandpass filter (1-45 Hz); Segmentation (10-second epochs); Autoreject toolbox (for bad epoch detection/cleaning); Exceptions: Autoreject excluded from ABCCT, femaleASD preprocessed and segmented into 2-second epochs, only downsampling and re-referencing.
rci_7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The 'Data preprocessing' section thoroughly details each step of the pipeline, including specific software and parameters, as well as exceptions for certain datasets.
rci_7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: The EEG preprocessing and artifact removal pipeline is executed through a multi-stage, fully automated algorithm. Initially, EEG signals undergo bandpass /uniFB01 ltering between 1 and 100 Hz... Signals were downsampled to 200 Hz. Bad EEG channels are identi /uniFB01 ed using the pyprep algorithm, which employs a RANSAC -based approach, and these channels are subsequently interpolated... Then, re-referencing is performed using the common average reference method... Independent Component Analysis (ICA) is then applied, and the IClabel algorithm automatically identi /uniFB01 es and rejects components related to eye blinks... A second bandpass /uniFB01 lter narrows the frequency range to 1 -45 Hz... The EEG signals are segmented into 10-second epochs... The Autoreject toolbox [50] is utilized for the detection and cleaning/rejection of bad epochs... Notably, the Autoreject step was excluded from the preprocessing of the ABCCT dataset. The femaleASD dataset had already been preprocessed and segmented into 2-second epochs. Therefore, further preprocessing for this dataset was con /uniFB01 ned solely to downsampling and re-referencing.

caa_8_key_findings_brief: EEG spectral and connectivity deviations from a normative population are extremely heterogeneous, challenging the case-control approach and emphasizing the need for individual variability in precision psychiatry.
caa_9_key_findings_detailed: The study revealed highly heterogeneous alterations, with deviation spatial overlap across patients not exceeding 40% for spectral power and 24% for connectivity. This heterogeneity challenges traditional case-control EEG studies, suggesting the inadequacy of one-size-fits-all approaches. The study demonstrated that incorporating individual deviations significantly enhanced comparative analysis and that patient-specific markers correlated with clinical assessments, such as ADOS scores, where increased ADOS scores were associated with increased positive global deviations and decreased negative global deviations. This represents a crucial step towards precision psychiatry through EEG.

caa_10_key_limitations.answer: Sample size (n ~ 2200) is large for EEG but smaller than MRI/fMRI studies and not broadly representative; non-uniform dataset sizes (HBN comprised 1539/2234 subjects, potentially biasing results); data from five studies using 128-channel EEG systems limits generalizability to other EEG systems; reliance on cross-sectional data limits assessment of within-subject variability and developmental trajectories; restricted age range (5-18 years) may contribute to observed heterogeneity, though similar patterns were found in an older population; inherent heterogeneity and comorbidity within patient groups pose challenges in isolating unique contributions; potential influence of medication on EEG results; choice of features modeled might not capture all homogeneity; GAMLSS limitations in training normative models for multiple response variables simultaneously, requiring individual models per channel/connection/region, calibrated to average values, and limiting rigorous representation of subject-level deviation.
caa_10_key_limitations.supporting_text: While our sample size is considered signi /uniFB01 cantly large for EEG studies (n ~ 2200), it does not reach the scale often seen in MRI and fMRI studies, nor is it representative of the broader population. Furthermore, the sample size of the datasets was not uniform. The largest dataset, HBN, comprised 1539 subjects out of the total 2234 subjects considered in this study, which could bias the results. Moreover, data for this article has been sourced from /uniFB01 ve studies (detailed in Methods) utilizing 128-channel EEG systems. While this somewhat controls for variability stemming from the spatial resolution of the collected EEG data, it also introduces limitations to the generalizability (over other EEG systems) of the results. In addition, our NM results are based on cross-sectional data, capturing individual deviations at a single time point. This limits our ability to assess within-subject variability and developmental trajectories. (...) One potential limitation is that the population included in the study has a restricted age range (5 -18 years), encompassing only younger, developmental stages. This may contribute to the observed heterogeneity, potentially due to varying developmental trajectories. However, in our recent study... we observed similar patterns of heterogeneity in a population aged over 40. (...) Another challenge of the study stems from the inherent heterogeneity that may exist within each group of patients who present multiple psychiatric diagnoses. This comorbidity (Table S1) introduces a layer of complexity. (...) Another limitation of this study is the potential in /uniFB01 uence of medication on EEG results in the assessed psychiatric patient cohort. (...) Our choice of the features to model was based on the most dominant features in the literature, however, it is plausible that alternative EEG features not included in our analysis could reveal greater homogeneity among the clinical groups. (...) Presently, the capability to train normative models for multiple response variables using GAMLSS is unavailable, thereby limiting modeling versatility. This constraint manifests in several ways. Firstly, individual models must be trained for each channel, connection, or region, escalating the complexity of both the procedure and its transition into a clinical tool. Secondly, these models are calibrated to the average values of respective channels, connections, or regions, potentially resulting in /uniFB01 tting inaccuracies for each model. Lastly, and notably, the inclusion of multiple response variables could yield a more rigorous representation of the deviation at the subject level.

caa_11_application_notes: The study leveraged normative models to derive individual EEG-markers, which outperformed classical features in differentiating between healthy controls and patient groups. This approach also provided a framework for generating subject-specific markers that correlated with clinical assessments, suggesting potential for delineating subgroups within diagnostic categories and informing personalized therapeutic interventions.
gn_1_general_note: The overall cohort size is 2234 individuals: 560 healthy controls (448 for training, 112 for testing) and 1674 clinically diagnosed participants. Resting-state HD-EEG (128 channels) data were recorded while participants had their eyes open. The entire cohort had an age range of 5-18 years (mean = 9.99 ± 3.06; 45% M). Ethical approval was provided by the Chesapeake Institutional Review Board, Yale Institutional Board (Yale, SCRI) and the Commission Cantonale d ' Ethique de la Recherche sur l ' e ̂ tre humain (CER-VD, Switzerland), with all procedures compliant with the 1964 Helsinki Declaration, and written informed consent obtained from all participants or their legal guardians.
